---
title: "Statistical Thinking report on published Australian Institute of Sport research from 2000 to 2024"
output: word_document
date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%d %B %Y')`"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, error=FALSE, comment='', dpi=400)
library(dplyr)
library(flextable)
library(tidyr)
library(janitor)
library(stringr)
library(xtable) # for exporting to latex
library(binom) # for intervals
source('99_functions.R') # for CI function
# plots:
library(ggplot2)
g.theme = theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
library(naniar) # for missing plots

# for search date
load('data/1_pubmed_papers.RData')
remove(data); pubmed_search_date = search_date

# all data sources, from 7_combine_data.R
load('data/7_analysis.RData') # 
```

Papers with AIS-supported authors were found by combining searches from papers found in _PubMed_ and _Scopus_ and a search provided by the AIS. The search was conducted on `r format(pubmed_search_date, '%d %B, %Y')`. The _OpenAlex_ database was searched on `r format(open_alex_search_date, '%d %B, %Y')`. 

## Methods

We use descriptive statistics with plots, tables and summary statistics. 
For summary statistics for continuous variables, we use the median and first to third quartile (Q1 to Q3). 
When confidence intervals are given for binomial data, we use the Wilson score interval to avoid any problems with the normal approximation given our relatively small sample size. 

## Papers by publication year

We included papers for the years 2020 to 2024.

```{r papers_year}
tab = mutate(open_alex_data, publication_year = as.numeric(format(date, '%Y'))) %>%
  group_by(publication_year) %>%
  tally()
# stats for big summary table
year_stats = mutate(open_alex_data, publication_year = as.numeric(format(date, '%Y'))) %>%
  summarise(q1 = quantile(publication_year, 0.25),
            median = median(publication_year),
            q3 = quantile(publication_year, 0.75)) %>%
  mutate(
    var = 'Year published', 
    stats = paste(median, ' [', q1, ' to ', q3, ']', sep='')) %>%
  select(-median, -q1, -q3) 
#
bplot = ggplot(data = tab, aes(x = publication_year, y = n))+
  geom_bar(stat='identity', col='grey22', size=0.1, fill='darkseagreen3')+
  xlab('Year')+
  ylab('Number of papers')+
  g.theme
bplot
```

The total number of papers is `r nrow(papers)`. The most papers were in 2020. The slight left skew towards earlier years is because papers with two dates (electronic and print) are shown using the earliest date. The double-dates for all papers means that some papers above have an earliest date prior to 2020.

# Section 1: Study design basics and authorship

## Study design (Q1a)

This question was evaluated by the research assistant.

```{r design}
#
tab = tabyl(type, type) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100)) %>%
  rename('Study design' = 'type') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# for summary table
stats_type = rename(tab, 'var' = 'Study design') %>%
  mutate(stats = paste(n, ' (', percent, ')', sep='')) %>%
  select('var', 'stats')
```

The "protocol" category was not in our study protocol, but was added after data collection.

The most common study design was an observational study. The "Other" category included audits, editorials, interviews, and position statements. 


#### Other study designs

The table below shows the other study designs that were used.

```{r other}
for_table = filter(type, type == 'Other') %>%
  mutate(
    comment = str_remove(comment, 'other, '),
    comment = str_remove(comment, ' study$'), # remove all 'study'
    comment = str_replace(comment, '^case$', 'case study'), #
    comment = str_replace(comment, 'concensus', 'consensus'),
    comment = str_replace(comment, 'qualitative study', 'interview'),
    comment = str_replace(comment, 'interview study', 'interview'))
tab = tabyl(for_table, comment) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100)) %>%
  rename('Other study type' = 'comment') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
```


## Author numbers per paper (Q1b)

This question was evaluated by the research assistant.

```{r anumbs}
# number of AIS authors
stats1 = summarise(ais_authors, N = n(), 
                   Min = min(number),
                   Q1 = round(quantile(number, 0.25)),
                   Median = round(quantile(number, 0.5)),
                   Q3 = round(quantile(number, 0.75)),
                   Max = round(max(number))) %>%
  mutate(Count = 'AIS authors')
# total number of authors
stats2 = summarise(ais_authors, N = n(), 
                   Min = min(total),
                   Q1 = round(quantile(total, 0.25)),
                   Median = round(quantile(total, 0.5)),
                   Q3 = round(quantile(total, 0.75)),
                   Max = round(max(total))) %>%
  mutate(Count = 'Total authors')
stats = bind_rows(stats1, stats2) %>%
  select(Count, everything()) # column ordering
ftab = flextable(stats) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# for summary table
stats_ais_authors = mutate(stats1, 
    stats = paste(Median, ' [', Q1, ' to ', Q3, ']', sep='')) %>%
  rename('var' = 'Count') %>%
  select('var', 'stats')
```

The table shows the summary statistics for the number of authors with an AIS affiliation and the total number of authors.

## Were the authors with an AIS affiliation in first or last position (Q1b)

This question was evaluated by the research assistant.

```{r first_last}
# 
tab1 = tabyl(ais_authors, first) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100)) %>%
  rename('Response' = 'first') %>%
  mutate('Position' = 'First') %>%
  filter(Response !='Total') # can remove total row as table 2 has the same total
tab2 = tabyl(ais_authors, last) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100)) %>%
  rename('Response' = 'last') %>%
  mutate('Position' = 'Last')
tab = bind_rows(tab1, tab2) %>%
  select(Position, Response, everything()) %>% # column ordering
  mutate(Response = case_when(
    Response == 'FALSE' ~ 'No',
    Response == 'TRUE' ~ 'Yes',
    Response == 'Total' ~ 'Total'
  ),
  Position = ifelse(Response=='Total', '', Position)) # separate total from either position
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  merge_v(j=1) %>%
  autofit()
ftab
```


First position is often seen as the author who has done the most work, whilst last position is often seen as the most senior author. 

## Was any author a statistician or methodologist? (Q1c)

This question was dropped from the analysis as we could not find a reliable automated method to identify statisticians and the manual method was too time consuming given the number of authors.

# Section 2: Research question(s) and/or study aim(s)

## Q2a: Did the paper have a well-formed research question or study aim? 

```{r well_formed_ex, include=FALSE}
n_exclude = filter(question, question == 'Not applicable') %>% nrow()
```

This question was evaluated by the research assistant.
We excluded `r n_exclude` papers where this was not applicable: an opinion piece and an infographic.

```{r well_formed}
for_table = filter(question, question != 'Not applicable')
N = nrow(for_table)
# 
tab = tabyl(for_table, question) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  rename('Well formed question' = 'question') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# numbers for summary diagram
summary_q2a = filter(tab, `Well formed question` == 'Yes') %>%
  mutate(qnum = 'q2a',
         qlabel  = 'Well-formed research question',
         Number = N)
# numbers for denominator diagram
denominator_q2a = data.frame(qnum = 'q2a',
         qlabel  = 'Well-formed research question',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5, # see 2 exclusions above
         protocol = 1,
         review = 1)
```

The category of "Purpose/Objective/Statement/Goal" was for papers that used a goal, objective, etc, instead of a research question. 
Most papers had a well-formed question or goal, although 20% without a well-formed question is still relatively large given the importance of stating a clear question. 

## Q2b: How many research questions or study aims were there?

```{r qnum_ex, include=FALSE}
n_exclude = filter(question_number, question == 'Not applicable') %>% nrow()
```

This question was evaluated by the research assistant. We excluded `r n_exclude` papers where the number of questions was not applicable, including those papers that did not have a well-formed question. 

```{r qnum}
# remove not applicable
for_table = filter(question_number, question != 'Not applicable')
# 
tab1 = tabyl(for_table, aims_n) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100)) %>%
  rename('Number' = 'aims_n') %>%
  mutate('Type' = 'Aims')
tab2 = tabyl(for_table, question_n) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100)) %>%
  rename('Number' = 'question_n') %>%
  mutate('Type' = 'Questions')
tab3 = tabyl(for_table, purpose_n) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100)) %>%
  rename('Number' = 'purpose_n') %>%
  mutate('Type' = 'Other')
# make columns
tab = bind_rows(tab1, tab2, tab3) %>%
  mutate(cell = paste(n, ' (', percent, ')', sep='')) %>%
  select(Type, Number, cell) %>% # column ordering
  mutate(Number = ifelse(is.na(Number), "Missing", Number)) %>%
  pivot_wider(values_from = 'cell', names_from = 'Type') %>%
  arrange(Number) %>%
  mutate(Aims = replace_na(Aims, '0'),
         Questions = replace_na(Questions, '0'),
         Other = replace_na(Other, '0'))
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# missing - none
any_missing = filter(for_table, is_na(aims_n) & is_na(purpose_n) & is_na(question_n)) %>% nrow()
```

After data collection, we added another category of "Other" because there were many papers that used a purpose, goal or objective instead of a research question or aim. 
Most papers had between 1 to 2 aims or questions. 

The table shows some missing for each type of question; however, there were no papers that were missing for all three types (aims, questions and other).

## Q2c: Can the question(s)/aim(s) be expressed using an established framework?

This question was evaluated by the research assistant. This information was often difficult to extract and there was a low inter-rater agreement in the random sample of 30 papers. Hence, we decided not to include this question in the main paper.


# Section 3: Prior research and planning

## Q3: Was there previous research on the same question(s) or aim(s)? (Did they cite a review or do their own review?) 

```{r prior_ex}
# 
# full_join(prior, type, by='doi') %>% filter(prior == 'Not applicable') %>% pull(comment)
n_exclude = filter(prior, prior == 'Not applicable') %>% nrow()
```

This question was evaluated by the research assistant. We excluded `r n_exclude` papers where this was not applicable, e.g., an opinion piece and an infographic.

```{r prior}
for_table = filter(prior, prior != 'Not applicable')
N = nrow(for_table)
# 
tab = tabyl(for_table, prior) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  rename('Previous research' = 'prior') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# numbers for summary diagram
summary_q3 = filter(tab, `Previous research` == 'Mentioned but this research justified') %>%
  mutate(qnum = 'q3',
         qlabel  = 'Research justified',
         Number = N)
# numbers for denominator diagram
# full_join(type, prior, by='doi') %>% group_by(prior, type) %>% tally()
denominator_q3 = data.frame(qnum = 'q3',
         qlabel  = 'Research justified',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5, # sometimes
         protocol = 1,
         review = 1)
```

Almost all papers (90%) mentioned previous research and gave a reason why this research was justified. 

## Q4a: Was there an analysis plan? 

```{r protocol_exclude, include = FALSE}
# exclude types that would not need a plan
pattern = 'infographic|statement|commentary|protocol|case study|primer|guidelines|consensus' # 
n_exclude = full_join(auto_data, type, by='doi') %>%
  filter(str_detect(comment, pattern)) %>%
  nrow()
# for text
exclude_text = str_split(pattern, '\\|')[[1]]
```

The data for this question was extracted using an automated search of the PDFs. We excluded `r n_exclude` papers that were one of: `r paste(exclude_text, collapse=', ')`.

In a change to our protocol, the study protocol question was dropped because for many papers in sports science the "protocol" means the training regimen; hence, there were many false positive matches. We were able to search for analysis plans. 


```{r protocol}
for_table = full_join(auto_data, type, by='doi') %>%
  filter(!str_detect(comment, pattern))
# 
N = nrow(for_table)
tab = tabyl(for_table, analysis_plan) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  rename('Analysis plan' = 'analysis_plan') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# numbers for summary diagram
summary_q4a = filter(tab, `Analysis plan` == TRUE) %>%
  mutate(qnum = 'q4a',
         qlabel  = 'Analysis plan', # not 'study protocol' because of change to our protocol
         Number = N) 
# numbers for denominator diagram
denominator_q4a = data.frame(qnum = 'q4a',
         qlabel  = 'Analysis plan',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5, # sometimes
         protocol = 0, # never included
         review = 1)
```

The results show that analysis plans were very rarely used.

## Q4b: Was the study pre-registered, e.g., ANZCTR or clintrials.gov?

The data for this question was extracted using an automated search of the PDFs. We excluded `r n_exclude` papers that were one of: `r paste(exclude_text, collapse=', ')`.

```{r anzctr}
# use same data as above with ineligible papers excluded
N = nrow(for_table)
# 
tab = tabyl(for_table, registration) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  rename('Pre-registered' = 'registration') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# numbers for summary diagram
summary_q4b = filter(tab, `Pre-registered` == TRUE) %>%
  mutate(qnum = 'q4b',
         qlabel  = 'Pre-registered',
         Number = N)
# numbers for denominator diagram; same as above
denominator_q4b = data.frame(qnum = 'q4b',
         qlabel  = 'Pre-registered',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5, # sometimes
         protocol = 0, # never included
         review = 1)
```

Few studies were pre-registered.

#### Pre-registration by study design

As pre-registration is more standard for experimental studies, the table below shows the percentages by study design.

```{r anzctr2}
# 
tab = tabyl(for_table, type, registration) %>%
  mutate(N = `TRUE` + `FALSE`,
    percent = round(`TRUE`/N*1000)/10,
    cell = paste(`TRUE`, '/', N, ' (', percent,')', sep='')) %>%
  select(type, cell) %>%
  rename('Study type' = 'type',
         'n/N (%)' = 'cell') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
```


# Section 4: Sample size

## Q5a: Was there a sample size calculation for the research question or study aim? 

This question was evaluated by the research assistant.
We excluded papers where this was not applicable, e.g., reviews.

```{r sample_size}
for_table = filter(sample_size, any_sample_size != 'Not applicable') 
N = nrow(for_table)
# 
tab = tabyl(for_table, any_sample_size) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  rename('Sample size calculation' = 'any_sample_size') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# numbers for summary diagram
summary_q5a = filter(tab, `Sample size calculation` == 'Yes') %>%
  mutate(qnum = 'q5a',
         qlabel  = 'Sample size calculation',
         Number = N)
# numbers for denominator diagram
denominator_q5a = data.frame(qnum = 'q5a',
         qlabel  = 'Sample size calculation',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5, # sometimes
         protocol = 1,
         review = 0)
```

Many studies did not give a sample size calculation. 

## Q5b: Was the effect size justified in the sample size calculation? 

This question was evaluated by the research assistant.
This was only for papers where the response to Q5a was "Yes".

```{r justified}
# need to merge two source because of conditional
for_table = full_join(sample_size, sample_size_justified, by='doi') %>%
  filter(any_sample_size == 'Yes')
N = nrow(for_table)
# 
tab = tabyl(for_table, sample_size_justified) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  rename('Effect size justified' = 'sample_size_justified') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# numbers for summary diagram
summary_q5b = filter(tab, `Effect size justified` == 'Yes') %>%
  mutate(qnum = 'q5b',
         qlabel  = 'Effect size justified in sample size calculation',
         Number = N)
# numbers for denominator diagram; same as above
denominator_q5b = data.frame(qnum = 'q5a',
         qlabel  = 'Effect size justified in sample size calculation',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5, # sometimes
         protocol = 1,
         review = 0)
```

Over half of studies with a sample size calculation provided a justification for the sample size. 

Some studies cited a previous study in their sample size calculation; we took classified this as not justifying the effect size as the citation needed to be supported by some reasoning from the authors. 

## Q5c: What was the target sample size? 

This question was evaluated by the research assistant. 
We only included papers that had a sample size calculation.

```{r target}
# could split by type (but too small)
for_stats_target = full_join(sample_size_target, sample_size, by='doi') %>%
  filter(any_sample_size == 'Yes')
#
stats_target = summarise(for_stats_target,
            N = n(), 
            Missing = sum(is.na(number)),
            Min = min(number, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q1 = round(quantile(number, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Median = round(quantile(number, 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Q3 = round(quantile(number, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Max = round(max(number, na.rm = TRUE))) 
ftab = flextable(stats_target) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# missing numbers for summary
missing_q5c = select(stats_target, Missing, N) %>% mutate(qnum = '5c')
# numbers for denominator diagram; same as above
denominator_q5c = data.frame(qnum = 'q5c',
         qlabel  = 'Target sample size',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5, # sometimes
         protocol = 0,
         review = 0)
```

Many target sample sizes were small with a median target sample size of just 18.

## Q5d: What was the actual sample size?

This question was evaluated by the research assistant.
We excluded papers where the sample size was not applicable (reviews, protocols, editorials, etc).

```{r actual}
#
for_stats_actual = select(sample_size_actual, -comment) %>%
  full_join(type, by='doi') %>%
  filter(!type %in% c('Protocol','Review'),
         !str_detect(comment, 'infographic|editorial|opinion|position|consensus'))
#
stats_actual = summarise(for_stats_actual,
            N = n(), 
            Missing = sum(is.na(number)),
            Min = min(number, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q1 = round(quantile(number, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Median = round(quantile(number, 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Q3 = round(quantile(number, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Max = round(max(number, na.rm = TRUE)))  
ftab = flextable(stats_actual) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# missing numbers for summary
missing_q5d = select(stats_actual, Missing, N) %>% mutate(qnum = '5d')
# export to latex
for_latex = bind_rows(stats_target, stats_actual, .id = 'sample') %>%
  mutate(sample = ifelse(sample == 1, "Target", 'Actual'))
print(xtable(for_latex, digits=0), include.rownames=FALSE, hline.after=FALSE, file = "reports/8_sample_size.tex")
# numbers for denominator diagram; same as above
denominator_q5d = data.frame(qnum = 'q5d',
         qlabel  = 'Actual sample size',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5, # sometimes
         protocol = 0,
         review = 0)
```

Many actual sample sizes were small with a median sample size of just 30.

#### Sample size by study design

The actual sample size can vary greatly by study design, hence we a boxplot to show the sample sizes by study type.

```{r actual_by_type, fig.height=4}
colours = c("cornsilk2", "aquamarine3", "dodgerblue")
bplot = ggplot(data = for_stats_actual, aes(x = factor(type), y = number, fill = factor(type)))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  scale_fill_manual(NULL, values = colours) + 
  scale_y_log10()+
  xlab(NULL)+
  ylab('Actual sample size')+
  coord_flip()+
  g.theme +
  theme(legend.position = 'none')
bplot

# version for paper
for_paper = bind_rows(sample_size_target, sample_size_actual, .id = 'stype') %>%
  full_join(type, by='doi') %>%
  filter(!type %in% c('Protocol','Review'),
         !str_detect(comment.y, 'infographic|editorial|opinion|position|consensus')) %>%
  mutate(x = case_when(
    type == 'Other' & stype == 1 ~ 1,
    type == 'Other' & stype == 2 ~ 2,
    type == 'Experimental study' & stype == 1 ~ 3,
    type == 'Experimental study' & stype == 2 ~ 4,
    type == 'Observational study' & stype == 1 ~ 5,
    type == 'Observational study' & stype == 2 ~ 6
  ))
# axis labels with numbers
xlabels = c("Other, target", "Other, actual", "Experimental study, target", "Experimental study, actual", "Observational study, target", "Observational study, actual")
medians = group_by(for_paper, x) %>%
  filter(!is.na(number)) %>%
  summarise(median = round(median(number)))
numbers = group_by(for_paper, x) %>%
  filter(!is.na(number)) %>% # remove missing
  tally() %>%
  left_join(medians, by = 'x') %>%
  mutate(label = xlabels,
         label = paste0(label, '\n(n=', n, ', Median = ', median,')'))
# colours with darker versions for target and actual
colours = c("cornsilk1","cornsilk3", "aquamarine1", "aquamarine3", "dodgerblue1", "dodgerblue3")
# plot
b2plot = ggplot(data = for_paper, aes(x = factor(x), y = number, fill = factor(x)))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  scale_fill_manual(NULL, values = colours) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = numbers$label)+
  scale_y_log10(limits=c(1,NA))+
  xlab(NULL)+
  ylab('Sample size')+
  geom_vline(xintercept=2.5, lty=2, col='grey77')+
  geom_vline(xintercept=4.5, lty=2, col='grey77')+
  coord_flip()+
  g.theme +
  theme(legend.position = 'none')
#
ggsave(plot = b2plot, filename = 'figures/8_sample_size.jpg', width = 5.8, height= 4.5, units = 'in', dpi=500)
```

Observational studies had generally larger sample size and had most of the very large studies.
The studies with a sample size of one were case studies. 
There were no experimental studies with a sample size over 100.

## Q5c and Q5d: Comparing the target and actual sample size

```{r actual_compare}
sizes = full_join(sample_size_target, sample_size_actual, by='doi') %>%
  rename('target' = 'number.x',
         'actual' = 'number.y')
# text
text1 = data.frame(target = 20, actual = 1000, text = 'Better than\nexpected')
text2 = data.frame(target = 100, actual = 10, text = 'Worse than\nexpected')
#
colours = c('darkorchid3','darkorange2')
gplot = ggplot(data = sizes, aes(x=target, y=actual))+
  geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1, lty=2, col='darkseagreen3')+ # 
  geom_point()+
  geom_label(data = text1, aes(x=target, y=actual, label=text))+
  geom_label(data = text2, aes(x=target, y=actual, label=text))+
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = colours) + 
  scale_x_log10()+
  scale_y_log10()+
  xlab('Target sample size')+
  ylab('Actual sample size')+
  geom_miss_point()+
  g.theme+
  theme(legend.position = "inside", 
        legend.position.inside =  c(0.85, 0.85))
gplot
```

The scatter plot compares the target and actual sample sizes. The studies that were missing a target sample size are shown using the purple dots on the left margin. 
The plot includes a diagonal line of agreement. 
We have used a log scale for both axes because of the strong positive skew in sample sizes with a few very large studies. 
There were more studies that exceeded their sample size than were under.

## Q6: How many participants were male and female? 

This question was evaluated by the research assistant. All tables and graphs below exclude the papers where gender was not applicable, e.g., reviews.

```{r gender_table}
#
for_table = left_join(gender, type, by = 'doi')
for_stats = filter(for_table, gender_not_applicable == FALSE) %>%
  filter(!type == 'Protocol') %>% # one protocol where planned numbers are given
  select(doi, female, male) %>%
  filter(female + male > 0) %>% # only those studies where there was a gender breakdown
  pivot_longer(-doi, values_to = 'number', names_to = 'gender') 
#
stats = group_by(for_stats, gender) %>%
  summarise(N = n(), 
            Missing = sum(is.na(number)),
            Min = min(number, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q1 = round(quantile(number, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Median = round(quantile(number, 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Q3 = round(quantile(number, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Max = round(max(number, na.rm = TRUE)))  
ftab = flextable(stats) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# numbers for denominator diagram; same as above
# full_join(type, gender, by='doi') %>% group_by(gender_not_applicable, type) %>% tally()
denominator_q6 = data.frame(qnum = 'q6',
         qlabel  = 'Male/female participants',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1, #
         other = 0.5, # sometimes
         protocol = 0,
         review = 0)
```

The table above shows the summary statistics on the number of males and females. We only show the statistics for those studies where information was given on the number of males and/or females.

```{r gender_plot}
n_removed = filter(gender, gender_not_applicable == TRUE | gender_not_reported  == TRUE) %>% nrow()
```

The scatter plot above aims to show the gender balance in studies. 
We removed `r n_removed` papers where gender was not applicable or not reported.
The plot axes are on the log scale because of the positive skew in the numbers of males and females. 
The dotted diagonal line indicates studies with equal numbers of men and women. The blue shaded area is a 20% difference in gender. 
The dots along the x- and y-axes are for single sex studies (see next table). 

### Number of single sex studies

```{r single_sex}
# remove not applicable and not reported
N = filter(gender, gender_not_applicable  == FALSE, gender_not_reported == FALSE) %>% nrow()
tab = filter(gender, gender_not_applicable  == FALSE, gender_not_reported == FALSE) %>%
  group_by(female_only, male_only) %>%
  tally() %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(percent = prop.table(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  mutate(Gender = case_when(
    female_only == FALSE & male_only == FALSE ~ 'Both',
    female_only == TRUE ~ 'Female only',
    male_only == TRUE ~ 'Male only',
    TRUE ~ 'Total'
  )) %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  select(Gender, n, percent, lower, upper)
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
```

Most studies were in both genders. There were slightly more studies in men only than women only.

# Section 5: Good reporting

## Q7: Was ethical clearance mentioned or was there a statement on why ethical clearance was not needed?  

The data for this question was extracted using an automated search of the PDFs. 
We removed reviews, commentaries, editorials, infographics.

```{r ethics}
# exclude types that would not need ethics
pattern = 'infographic|statement|commentary|protocol|primer|guidelines|consensus' # 
for_table = full_join(auto_data, type, by='doi') %>%
  filter(!str_detect(comment, pattern))  %>%
  filter(type != 'Review') 
N = nrow(for_table)
# 
tab = tabyl(for_table, ethics) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  rename('Ethics statement' = 'ethics') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab 
# numbers for summary diagram

  mutate(qnum = 'q7',
         qlabel  = 'Ethics statement',
         Number = N)
# numbers for denominator diagram
denominator_q7 = data.frame(qnum = 'q7',
         qlabel  = 'Ethics statement',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5, # 
         protocol = 1, 
         review = 0)
```

Most studies included a statement regard ethics approval, which includes stating why ethical approval was not needed. 
Some statements on ethical approval did not include the date or approval number, but both would ideally be included to provide the most transparency. 
The ethics committees mentioned are shown in the appendix below. 

## Q8. Were the data openly shared?

The data for this question was extracted using an automated search of the PDFs. 
The original question in the protocol was "Was there a data availability statement?"; however, we changed this to the more strict criterion of whether the data was openly shared. This is a stronger test of transparency. 
We removed studies types that would not include original data to share, including protocols, editorials, opinions, or commentaries.

```{r data}
# exclude types that would not need to share data
pattern = 'infographic|statement|commentary|protocol|case study|primer|guidelines|consensus' # 
for_table = full_join(open_data_results, type, by='doi') %>%
  filter(!str_detect(comment, pattern))
N = nrow(for_table)
# 
tab = tabyl(for_table, is_open_data) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  rename('Data statement' = 'is_open_data') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# numbers for summary diagram
summary_q8 = filter(tab, `Data statement` == TRUE) %>%
  mutate(qnum = 'q8',
         qlabel  = 'Openly available data',
         Number = N)
# numbers for denominator diagram
denominator_q8 = data.frame(qnum = 'q8',
         qlabel  = 'Openly available data',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5, # not editorial
         protocol = 1, 
         review = 1)
```

Very few studies openly shared data. We manually checked the five papers that assessed to have open data and there was a stated use of a data despository for every paper. However, we did not download the data and check if the data matched those used in the paper. 

If the data were stated by the authors to be 'available on request' then this was not clased as open data.

## Q11: Were outliers removed without justification?

This question was evaluated by the research assistant. We excluded papers where outliers were unlikely to be relevant, e.g. protocols and reviews. 

```{r outliers}
for_table = filter(outliers, outliers != 'Not applicable')
N = nrow(for_table)
# 
tab = tabyl(for_table, outliers) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  rename('Outliers' = 'outliers') 
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# numbers for summary diagram, 
summary_q11 = mutate(for_table, 
                     frame = case_when( # make into simpler yes/no (so all frameworks are yes)
                       outliers == 'Yes, no justification' ~ 'No',
                       TRUE ~ 'Yes' # otherwise (all other categories are good)
                     )) %>%
  tabyl(frame) %>%
  adorn_totals(where='row') %>%
  add_intervals(N = N) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(percent*100),
         lower = round(lower*100),
         upper = round(upper*100)) %>%
  filter(frame == 'Yes') %>%
  mutate(qnum = 'q11',
         qlabel  = 'Outliers not removed or removed with justification',
         Number = N)
# numbers for denominator diagram
# full_join(type, outliers, by='doi') %>% group_by(outliers, type) %>% tally()
denominator_q11 = data.frame(qnum = 'q11',
         qlabel  = 'Outliers not removed or removed with justification',
         experimental = 1,
         observational = 1,
         other = 0.5,  
         protocol = 0, 
         review = 0)
```

Most papers did not remove outliers. When outliers were removed, there were seven papers that did this without justification. An example quote is "one athlete was removed from the final analysis as the subject was identified as an extreme outlier". This is not an adequate justification for exclusion as outliers can occur in real data and exclusions should only occur for data that is believed to be an error.

# Summary diagram

The diagram below summarises the questions in an attempt to show where authors are generally doing well and where improvements could be made. The plot is ordered with the best performing questions at the top. The results are coloured in two groups, those above 60% classed as relatively good (blue) and those under 40% classed as relatively bad (red).

```{r summary, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
# combine summaries (means and CIs)
for_plot_summary = bind_rows(#summary_q1c, # dropped
                     summary_q2a, 
                     #summary_q2c, # excluded after poor inter-rater agreement
                     summary_q3,
                     summary_q4a,
                     summary_q4b,
                     summary_q5a,
                     summary_q5b,
                     summary_q6x, # gender reported
                     summary_q7,
                     summary_q8,
                     summary_q9a,
                     summary_q9b,
                     summary_q10,
                     summary_q11,
                     summary_q12,
                     summary_q13,
                     summary_q14a,
                     summary_q14b,
                     summary_q14c) %>% 
  select(qnum, qlabel, n, Number, percent, lower, upper) %>%
  arrange(percent) %>% # arrange questions by percent
  mutate(x = 1:n(),
         comb_label = paste(qnum, '. ', qlabel, sep=''),
         comb_label = str_remove(comb_label, '^q'), # remove q at start
         colour = case_when( # colour by percent
           percent >= 60 ~ 1, # best
           percent >= 40 ~ 2, # grey zone
           percent < 40 ~ 3 # worse
         ))
colours = c('darkseagreen4','grey55','darkred') # high, medium, low
colours = c('darkseagreen4','darkred') # high, low - no means in the medium
# 
n_plot = nrow(for_plot_summary)
splot = ggplot(data = for_plot_summary, aes(x = x, y = percent, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, colour =  factor(colour))) +
  geom_point()+
  scale_color_manual(NULL, values = colours)+
  scale_x_continuous(expand = 0.02, breaks = 1:n_plot, labels = for_plot_summary$comb_label)+
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,100))+
  geom_errorbar(width=0, linewidth=1.05)+
#  geom_text()+
  g.theme+
  theme(legend.position = 'none',
        font = element_text(size = 16))+
  xlab(NULL)+
  ylab('Percent')+
  coord_flip()
splot
# export
ggsave(plot = splot, filename = 'figures/8_summary_diagram.jpg', width=5.5, height=5.4, units='in', dpi=500)
```

```{r common_journals}
  arrange(desc(n))%>%
  mutate(percent = round(100*n / N),
         n = paste(n, ' (', percent, ')', sep='')) %>%
  slice(1:10) %>%
  select(-percent)
names(tab)[1] = 'Journal'
top_3_journals = slice(tab, 1:3) %>% # for summary table
  rename('var' = 'Journal',
         'stats' = 'n')
ftab = flextable(tab) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
```

## Papers published in Frontiers or MDPI

This uses data from _OpenAlex_.

```{r frontiers}
spub = c("Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute","Frontiers Media")
selected_publishers = filter(open_alex_data, publisher %in% spub) %>%
  select(journal, title) %>%
  arrange(journal, title)
ftab = flextable(selected_publishers) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  width(j=1, width=5, unit='cm') %>%
  width(j=2, width=13, unit='cm') 
ftab
```

There were `r nrow(selected_publishers)` papers published in _MDPI_ or _Frontiers_ journals.

_MDPI_ and _Frontiers_ are considered as predatory publishers by [an independent group of researchers](https://www.predatoryjournals.org/the-list/publishers). Both publishers were clear outliers in [an analysis of publication patterns over time](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15884) with an enormous recent increase in output and special issues. They also have fast turn-around times, which raises concern about the rigor of their peer review.


Summary statistics on the number of authors per paper.

## Citations

The citation data were from _OpenAlex_.

#### Summary statistics for citation counts

```{r cite_stats}
# adjusted to per year
citations = select(open_alex_data, doi, date, cited) %>%
  mutate(time = as.numeric(as.Date('2025-08-21') - date), # citation search to publication date
         yearly = cited / (time/365.25)) # citations per year
#
for_stats =  pivot_longer(citations, cols = c(cited, yearly))
stats = group_by(for_stats, name) %>%
  summarise(      N = n(), 
                  Missing = sum(is.na(value)),
                  Min = min(value),
                  Q1 = round(quantile(value, 0.25)),
                  Median = round(quantile(value, 0.5)),
                  Q3 = round(quantile(value, 0.75)),
                  Max = round(max(value))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename('Type' = 'name')
ftab = flextable(stats) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# stats for big summary table
citation_stats = mutate(stats, 
    var = c('Total citations','Citations per year'), 
    stats = paste(Median, ' [', Q1, ' to ', Q3, ']', sep='')) %>%
  select(var, stats) 
```

Total citations counts and counts per year.

#### Histogram of adjusted citation counts

```{r citations}
cplot = ggplot(data = citations, aes(yearly))+
  geom_histogram(fill = 'darkseagreen2', col = 'grey77')+
  xlab('Citations per year')+
  ylab('Count')+
  g.theme
cplot
```

We look at the citations per year to adjust for time since publication (as papers published recently have less time to accrue citations). The distribution has a strong positive skew, with a few highly cited papers.

Summary statistics on _Altmetric_ scores. The highest _Altmetric_ score was for the paper titled "`r paper_max$title`" published in _`r paper_max$journal`_.

# Summary tables

## Descriptive statistics

```{r summary_table}
# year, top three topics, top three journals
big_table = bind_rows(year_stats,
                      stats_ais_authors,
                      citation_stats,
                      altmetric_stats,
                      stats_type,
                      top_3_topics, 
                      top_3_journals,
                      .id = 'group') %>%
  select(group, var, stats) %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(
    group == 1 ~ '',
    group == 2 ~ '',
    group == 3 ~ '',
    group == 4 ~ '',
    group == 5 ~ 'Study design',
    group == 6 ~ 'Topics (top 3)',
    group == 7 ~ 'Journals (top 3)',
  )) %>%
  filter(var != 'Total') # remove total row
ftab = flextable(big_table) %>%
  merge_v(j=1) %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit()
ftab
# export to latex
print(xtable(big_table), include.rownames=FALSE, hline.after=FALSE, file = "reports/8_big_table.tex")
```

## Question denominators

The tile plot below shows which studies were included for which questions. For example, reviews are not expected to have a sample size calculation and so were excluded for that question. The ``Other'' study category included a wide mix of studies and hence whether these studies were included often depended on more detailed information. This meant that the Other study category often included a mix of included and excluded papers.

```{r denominator}
# get numbers for axis label
label_stats = group_by(type, type) %>% 
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  mutate(name = case_when(  # for merge
    type == 'Experimental study' ~ 'experimental',
    type == 'Observational study' ~ 'observational',
    type == 'Other' ~ 'other',
    type == 'Protocol' ~ 'protocol',
    type == 'Review' ~ 'review'
  ))
# combine summaries (means and CIs)
for_plot_denominator = bind_rows(
  denominator_q2a, 
  denominator_q3,
  denominator_q4a,
  denominator_q4b,
  denominator_q5a,
  denominator_q5b,
  denominator_q5c,
  denominator_q5d,
  denominator_q6,
  denominator_q7,
  denominator_q8,
  denominator_q9a,
  denominator_q9b,
  denominator_q10,
  denominator_q11,
  denominator_q12,
  denominator_q13,
  denominator_q14a,
  denominator_q14b,
  denominator_q14c) %>% 
  mutate(x = 1:n()) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(x, qnum, qlabel)) %>%
  mutate(comb_label = paste(qnum, '. ', qlabel, sep=''),
        comb_label = str_remove(comb_label, '^q')) %>%
  left_join(label_stats, by='name') %>%
  mutate(name = paste(str_to_sentence(name),'\n(n = ', n, ')', sep=''))
colours = c('azure','skyblue','navy') # not used, sometimes, used
# 
labels = select(for_plot_denominator, x, comb_label) %>% unique()
dplot = ggplot(data = for_plot_denominator, aes(x = x, y = name, fill = factor(value))) +
  geom_tile(col = 'grey77')+
  scale_fill_manual("Included", labels=c('No','Partial','Yes'), values = colours)+
  scale_x_reverse(expand = 0, breaks = 1:nrow(labels), labels = labels$comb_label)+
  scale_y_discrete(expand = 0)+
  g.theme+
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
    font = element_text(size = 16))+
  xlab(NULL)+
  ylab(NULL)+
  coord_flip()
dplot
# export
ggsave(plot = dplot, filename = 'figures/8_denominator_diagram.jpg', width=6.5, height=5.4, units='in', dpi=500)
```

For Q14, there were some papers that were excluded because they did not have a research question or aim. This included some experimental and observational studies, although they were not excluded based on the study type.
